P1: The January 14, 2026 rename added Async to 46 yielding methods. Player:LoadCharacter is now LoadCharacterAsync, BadgeService:AwardBadge is now AwardBadgeAsync, and MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo is now GetProductInfoAsync. The old names are only informationally deprecated. They behave the same, no removal is scheduled, and they still work, but new code should use the Async names inside pcall. Instance:WaitForChild and RemoteFunction:InvokeServer were not renamed, so they are still the current names.
P2: Set Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server (full release July 9, 2026). This forces several settings on: NextGenerationReplication, Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem, SignalBehavior = Deferred, StreamingEnabled and UseFixedSimulation. Put gameplay logic that the client predicts and the server re-simulates in a function bound with RunService:BindToSimulation(fn). Keep it deterministic, because it can re-run on rollback/resimulation. Don't call Destroy or reparent inside it, and read input through InputAction state. Use time() as the clock, not tick(), os.time() or os.clock(). Limits: only the first 64 attributes replicate, and names and strings are capped at 50 characters. Note that SetNetworkOwner is not an equivalent mechanism.
P3:
The property is Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem.
- Phase 1 (June 2026): opt-in, default Disabled.
- Phase 2 (planned early 2027): default Enabled.
- Phase 3 (planned mid 2027): the property is removed and the legacy scripts are gone.
Server Authority mode already forces it on.

Code at risk of breaking:
- Anything that reaches into PlayerModule internals, for example require(PlayerModule):GetControls() or the control/camera modules.
- Code that relies on the old ContextActionService/UserInputService input sinking, for example binding over default movement keys.
- Forked or edited copies of the default PlayerScripts. Forks need StarterPlayer.CreateDefaultPlayerModule = Disabled.

P5:
Since the July 29, 2026 unification, in-game and Open Cloud requests share one budget per experience for each request type.
- Writes: 300 + 20 x CCU per minute.
- Reads: 300 + 40 x CCU per minute.
- UpdateAsync costs 1 read + 1 write, so it spends from both budgets.
- Per-server limits (60 + 40 x players for writes) still exist but are secondary.
- Per-key throughput: 4 MB/min write and 25 MB/min read on a rolling 60 s window. Each request is rounded up to the next KB.
- Request queues hold 30 requests. Overflow fails with errors 301-306.
- Storage: 500 MB + 1 MB x lifetime users, measured compressed, counting only the latest version.
- Check GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before bursts. The old 6-second-per-key rule no longer applies.

G1:
ProcessReceipt correctness rules:
- Set exactly one ProcessReceipt callback, on the server.
- Make it idempotent per receiptInfo.PurchaseId. Record granted PurchaseIds in a DataStore (or in session-locked player data), and if an ID is already recorded, return PurchaseGranted without granting again.
- Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant has been durably saved.
- If the player is not in the server, the product is unknown, the data isn't loaded, or the save failed or threw, return NotProcessedYet. Roblox then retries later, for example when the player rejoins.
- Never yield forever, and wrap DataStore calls in pcall.

Charged but nothing received: the callback returned PurchaseGranted even though the save failed, or the player had left. It can also error or return nil and the grant is lost.
Item received twice: there was no PurchaseId check. Roblox retries any receipt that wasn't acknowledged, for example when the server crashed after granting but before returning, or when it returned NotProcessedYet after granting. Read-modify-write SetAsync races make this worse. Use UpdateAsync so the grant and the PurchaseId record are saved atomically.
G2:
Use UpdateAsync whenever the new value depends on the old one, or when several servers could write the same key. Examples are currency changes, session locks, receipt records, and save-on-leave racing a teleport. SetAsync blindly overwrites, so a stale server can clobber newer data. Plain SetAsync is fine only for a first-time or unconditional write.

Rules for the transform function:
- It must not yield. No waits and no other DataStore calls.
- It may run several times on a conflict, so it must be pure and deterministic with no side effects such as granting items or firing remotes. Do those after the call succeeds.
- Return the new value, or return nil to cancel the write.
- Treat the old value as possibly nil (new player) or newer than you expected.
- Don't mutate shared tables you'll use outside it.
- Wrap the call in pcall with retry and backoff.

UpdateAsync costs 1 read + 1 write against the budgets.
G3:
It is not safe. typeof(gold) == "number" accepts NaN, inf and fractional values.
- NaN fails every comparison, so NaN < 0 and NaN > Gold are both false and the check passes.
- Fractions like 0.5 or 1e-9 get through.
- It also only checks the balance when the offer is created, not when the trade executes. A player can offer their gold on several trades, or spend it before acceptance, and duplicate gold.

Fix:
```lua
offerRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
    if typeof(gold) ~= "number" or gold ~= gold then return end -- NaN
    if gold ~= math.floor(gold) or gold < 1 or gold > 1e9 then return end
    if not rateLimit(player) then return end
    if gold > player.Gold.Value then return end
    createOffer(player, gold)
end)
```
When the trade completes, re-validate atomically on the server: re-check both balances and escrow (deduct) the gold when the offer is made or locked. Keep the balance in server data, not in a value the client could influence. Cap open offers per player.
G4:
Each frame the Animator writes joint Transforms during its step, which runs before PreSimulation, physics and Heartbeat. The Animator overwrites Motor6D.Transform with the animated pose every frame. A Heartbeat write happens after the Animator, so the next frame's animation step replaces it before it is ever simulated or rendered with the idle pose.

Write procedural offsets in RunService.PreSimulation (formerly Stepped). That runs after the Animator has set this frame's pose. Compose with the animated value instead of replacing it:
```lua
RunService.PreSimulation:Connect(function()
    motor.Transform = aimRotation * motor.Transform -- applies on top of the clip
end)
```
Don't accumulate across frames with Transform = Transform * offset when nothing keys the joint, because it compounds.

Edit C0 instead only for a persistent rest-pose offset. The Animator never writes C0, so a C0 change survives animations. Examples are a permanent mount offset, or a whole turret where nothing animates that joint. The trade-off is that you must clean C0 up yourself and it can fight retargeting. Transform changes made on the client are local, so replicate the aim angle and let each client apply it.
G5:
Roblox resolves animation conflicts per joint. A track only competes on the joints it actually keys.
- Higher AnimationPriority wins. The order is Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2 < Action3 < Action4.
- On each joint, the highest-priority playing tracks take weight first. Lower priorities get only the remaining weight, up to a total of 1.
- Tracks at the same priority blend in proportion to their weights.

Common causes of a weak swing:
- The swing was left at Core or Movement priority (the same as walk), so it gets averaged 50/50 with walk, or loses.
- It was played with a low weight. For example, with Action at weight 0.6, walk still gets the other 40%.
- The swing doesn't key the arm joints you expect.

Fix: set the animation's priority to Action (or higher) in the editor or with track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action, and play it at full weight with track:Play(fadeTime, 1). AdjustWeight changes the weight at runtime. Weight is the target weight and fadeTime is the blend time. If the total weight on a joint is below 1 and nothing is underneath, the pose blends toward rest.
G6:
The size is a unit-chain mismatch. Blender works in meters with Unit Scale 1.0, but FBX stores centimeters. With the default "All Local" apply-scaling setting, the scale factor of 100 is baked in. Studio's importer then reads the file's units, and the model ends up 100x too large. Small Unit Scale settings like 0.01 cause the same problem.

Recommended settings:
- Keep the Blender scene at metric with Unit Scale 1.0 (don't change it mid-project).
- In the FBX export, set Apply Scalings to "FBX Unit Scale". Keep Scale at 1.0 and apply object scale and rotation (Ctrl+A) before export.
- Use forward -Z, up Y. Enable Apply Transform where appropriate. Export only the selected mesh and armature.
- In the Studio 3D Importer, set the file's units/Scale Unit to Studs (or Meters) and check the preview against an R15 avatar, which is about 5 studs tall.
- Alternatively, export glTF/GLB, which is defined in meters.

Don't rescale rigged models in Studio, because the animation translations stay in the old units.
G7:
Mirror and Bevel are non-destructive modifiers. Your .glb was exported with only the base cage, meaning modifiers weren't applied (the glTF exporter's Apply Modifiers option was off). That leaves half the mesh with no bevel geometry, so the edges are sharp.

Fix: enable Apply Modifiers in the glTF exporter, or apply the stack manually on a copy (top to bottom). For Mirror, use Clipping and put the origin on the symmetry plane. Then Merge by Distance and recalculate normals.

The catch: Apply Modifiers can't be combined with an armature or skinning. On a rigged mesh, applying modifiers drops or breaks the Armature modifier and skin weights, and shape keys are lost too. Only use it on static props. For rigged meshes, apply Mirror and Bevel manually before rigging, or on a duplicate, and keep only the Armature modifier live. Also, some Blender versions lose custom normals from Weighted Normal or Harden Normals during the conversion, so check the shading afterward.
G8:
Problem 1: UDim2.fromScale(0.3, 0.3) is 30% of the screen width and 30% of the height. Screens have different aspect ratios, so the frame's shape changes. Fixes:
- Add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (for example AspectRatio = 1, or your design ratio, with AspectType = FitWithinMaxSize).
- Or set SizeConstraint = RelativeYY so the width scales off the height.
- Pair this with UISizeConstraint or UIScale for min and max sizes.

Problem 2: the ScreenGui's insets allow content under the notch and the top bar. This happens with IgnoreGuiInset = true, ScreenInsets = None or DeviceSafeInsets, or the legacy safe-area behavior. Fixes:
- Set ScreenGui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets for interactive HUD elements. This keeps them clear of the notch and the Roblox top bar buttons.
- Set SafeAreaCompatibility = None on new GUIs.
- Anchor the button with AnchorPoint (0,0) and a small offset. Use GuiService:GetGuiInset() / TopbarInset only if you position manually.
- Put full-screen backgrounds in a separate ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = None.

```lua
local ItemConfig = require(game.ServerStorage.ItemConfig) -- server-owned prices
local BuyItem = RS.Remotes.BuyItem
local lastBuy = {}

BuyItem.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
    -- rate limit
    local now = os.clock()
    if lastBuy[player] and now - lastBuy[player] < 0.25 then return end
    lastBuy[player] = now
    -- type + range validation (rejects NaN, inf, fractions)
    if typeof(itemId) ~= "string" or #itemId > 50 then return end
    if typeof(quantity) ~= "number" or quantity ~= quantity
        or quantity ~= math.floor(quantity) or quantity < 1 or quantity > 99 then return end
    local item = ItemConfig[itemId]
    if not item then return end
    local data = PlayerData.get(player) -- server-authoritative profile
    if not data then return end
    local cost = item.Price * quantity
    if data.Coins < cost then return end
    data.Coins -= cost
    data.Inventory[itemId] = (data.Inventory[itemId] or 0) + quantity
    PlayerData.markDirty(player)
end)

game.Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) lastBuy[p] = nil end)
```
The price comes from the server and never from the client. The deduction and grant happen in the same server step with no yields between them.
T2:
```lua
-- Profile key: "Player_"..userId -> {Data=..., Lock={JobId=, Time=}}
local LOCK_TTL = 1800 -- s; stale lock = crashed server
function load(player)
  for attempt = 1, 5 do
    local ok, result = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(old)
      old = old or {Data = defaultData(), Lock = nil}
      local lock = old.Lock
      if lock and lock.JobId ~= game.JobId and os.time() - lock.Time < LOCK_TTL then
        return nil -- locked by another server: cancel write
      end
      old.Lock = {JobId = game.JobId, Time = os.time()}
      return old
    end)
    if ok and result and result.Lock.JobId == game.JobId then
      return result.Data -- we own the session
    end
    task.wait(attempt * 2) -- previous server still saving (teleport/rejoin)
  end
  player:Kick("Data still in use, please rejoin") -- never play with unlocked data
end

function save(player, release) -- autosave every 60s (dirty only) + on leave
  pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(old)
    if not old or not old.Lock or old.Lock.JobId ~= game.JobId then return nil end -- lost lock: don't overwrite
    old.Data = sessionData[player]
    old.Lock = (not release) and {JobId = game.JobId, Time = os.time()} or nil
    return old
  end)
end
-- PlayerRemoving -> save(p, true); BindToClose -> save all with release, wait for completion.
-- Teleport: save + release BEFORE TeleportAsync; destination load() waits/retries for the lock.
```
Trades and grants only modify the locked session data. Purchases are recorded by PurchaseId.

T4:
On the server, OnServerEvent always passes the firing player as the first argument automatically. The client also passed LocalPlayer explicitly, so the server receives (player, LocalPlayer, 50). amount is therefore the Player Instance, and amount + 1 errors.

Fix the client by not sending the player:
```lua
remote:FireServer(50)
```
The server stays the same, but validate the value:
```lua
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, amount)
    if typeof(amount) ~= "number" or amount ~= amount then return end
    print(amount + 1)
end)
```
Never trust a player argument sent by the client. Always use the automatic first parameter.
T5:
In Studio solo play, the player can join before the server Script runs. That happens when the script is slow to load, yields (for example, require or WaitForChild) before connecting, or is under Deferred signal behavior. PlayerAdded has already fired for that player, so the handler never runs for them. Live servers usually start before anyone joins, which hides the race.

The standard fix is to connect the handler, then loop over the players who are already in the game:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local function onPlayerAdded(player)
    local ls = Instance.new("Folder")
    ls.Name = "leaderstats"
    local coins = Instance.new("IntValue")
    coins.Name = "Coins"
    coins.Parent = ls
    ls.Parent = player
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do
    task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p)
end
```
Also connect before any yields at the top of the script. The folder must be named exactly "leaderstats".

T8:
Your game almost certainly has Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLoDs set to Enabled (the newer default). In that mode every MeshPart uses mesh streaming with cloud-generated LoDs, and RenderFidelity is ignored. The property is also planned for removal. So setting it to Precise does nothing, and detail still drops at a distance.

What to do:
- Check that Workspace property first.
- To control quality, budget triangles at the source and author clean meshes.
- Keep important hero meshes reasonably dense, since LoD falls back based on distance and screen size.
- Don't rely on RenderFidelity.
- If you turn the Workspace setting off, RenderFidelity applies again (Automatic, Precise or Performance), but you lose streaming and improved LoDs.

Test in the published client, not just in Studio.
